description:
FILED s440 from agent D's #503 report (pre-existing, loud, unrelated to #503). Repro: `print "c3 [", (sub { return "x" })->(), "\n";`. The parenthesised anon-sub term takes the LIST path (a vector) before the `->()` postfix; the `->(` on a parenthesised single expression must unwrap to the expression itself (the #411 elided-arrow family / `(EXPR)->()` shape). Bar: the repro + `(sub {...})->(1,2)` + `(sub {...})->()->()` + `(\&f)->()` + `(sub{...}, sub{...})[1]->()` vs perl; a row in the anon-sub topical file.

DONE s443h (Opus, agent H round 4), commits 57c9859/8d468b7, ff-merged s444.  `->(` joins ExprToCL's paren-scalar-base family (the fourth member; it never asked _is_paren_scalar_base), so `(sub {...})->()` in LIST context stopped dying.  Fable re-probed the four bar shapes incl. (\&f)->() and the slice form -- identical to perl.  RESIDUE = #527 (multi-element paren base, all four family members).
subject: `(sub { ... })->()` -- an immediately-called anon-sub LITERAL -- dies "Not a CODE reference" and kills the whole file: the emission is `(p-funcall-ref (vector (lambda ...)))` and %p-wrong-referent-p rejects the vector (`my $c = sub {...}; $c->()` works)
